title: The fixed unit of an exact-derived adjunction commutes with cochain shifts
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories with ordinary unbounded derived categories and localization functors $Q_{\mathcal A},Q_{\mathcal B}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $L:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $P:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ be additive exact functors with a specified adjunction $L\dashv P$, unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$. Let $C(L),C(P)$ denote termwise application on cochain complexes, and $L_D,P_D$ their exact-derived functors with the standard localization and shift comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Use the specified adjunction $L_D\dashv P_D$ obtained by localizing the degreewise adjunction [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction], rather than an arbitrarily chosen adjunction between the same functors. For every $a\in\mathbf Z$ let $e_L^{(a)}:C(L)(X[a])\to C(L)(X)[a]$ and $e_P^{(a)}:C(P)(Y[a])\to C(P)(Y)[a]$ be the identity in every degree. These are natural isomorphisms of complexes with the canonical compatibility under $[a][b]\cong[a+b]$ and $[0]\cong\mathrm{id}$: their degree-$m$ terms are $L(X^{m+a})$, respectively $P(Y^{m+a})$, and their differentials are $(-1)^aL(d_X^{m+a})=L((-1)^ad_X^{m+a})$, respectively the analogous expression for $P$. The degreewise unit is a cochain map whose degree-$m$ component at $X[a]$ is $\eta_{X^{m+a}}$, and satisfies
$$C(\eta)_X[a]=e_{P,C(L)X}^{(a)}\,C(P)(e_{L,X}^{(a)})\,C(\eta)_{X[a]}.$$
Write $\eta^D$ for the localized unit and $\bar e_L,\bar e_P$ for the fixed induced comparisons. Then, as an equality of natural transformations on the entire derived category,
$$\eta^D_X[a]=\bar e_{P,L_DX}^{(a)}\,P_D(\bar e_{L,X}^{(a)})\,\eta^D_{X[a]}.$$
The assertion uses the fixed termwise right comparison, with no monoidal, boundedness, K-injective-preservation or resolution hypothesis beyond the stated existence of the derived categories.

proof.text: Fix $a\in\mathbf Z$. For either $F=L$ or $F=P$, additivity gives $F((-1)^a d)=(-1)^aF(d)$. Thus the identity on $F(X^{m+a})$ is a cochain isomorphism $e_F^{(a)}$ with inverse the same degreewise identity. Its naturality is the equality $F(f^{m+a})=F(f^{m+a})$. The zero comparison is the identity, and under the canonical reindexing $(X[a])[b]\cong X[a+b]$ both composites for the addition comparison are identities on $F(X^{m+a+b})$; their differentials agree since $(-1)^a(-1)^b=(-1)^{a+b}$. These are exactly the termwise comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], not newly chosen comparisons.

proof.text: Write $H=C(P)C(L)$ and $u_X=C(\eta)_X:X\to HX$. Naturality of the given abelian unit at $d_X^m$ says $P(L(d_X^m))\eta_{X^m}=\eta_{X^{m+1}}d_X^m$, which is precisely the cochain-map condition. At $X[a]$ the same equation holds with differential $(-1)^a d_X^{m+a}$, by additivity. Put $e_X=e_{P,C(L)X}^{(a)}\circ C(P)(e_{L,X}^{(a)})$. Both $u_X[a]$ and $e_Xu_{X[a]}$ have degree-$m$ component $\eta_{X^{m+a}}$, because the two comparisons are identities and $P$ preserves identities. Hence $u_X[a]=e_Xu_{X[a]}$ as cochain maps. For a cochain map $f$, naturality of $u$ is the original naturality of $\eta$ at each $f^m$; therefore this is an equality of natural transformations, before localization.

proof.text: Let $Q=Q_{\mathcal A}$, $H_D=P_DL_D$ and $t_X:Q(X[a])\xrightarrow{\sim}(QX)[a]$ be the localization shift comparison. Let $\varphi_{L,X}:L_DQX\cong Q_{\mathcal B}C(L)X$ and $\varphi_{P,Y}:P_DQ_{\mathcal B}Y\cong QC(P)Y$ be the fixed comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], and define $\kappa_X=\varphi_{P,C(L)X}\circ P_D(\varphi_{L,X}):H_DQX\cong QHX$. The specified localized adjunction [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction] has precisely the localized degreewise unit; in these coordinates this says $\kappa_X\eta^D_{QX}=Q(u_X)$. In particular this formula concerns the given unit, not merely a unit for some adjunction on the same pair of functors.

source.place: paragraph on adjunction units and counits; agent expansion, step 3

proof.text:
Put $s_Z=\bar e_{P,L_DZ}^{(a)}\circ P_D(\bar e_{L,Z}^{(a)})$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], applied to $P$ at $C(L)X$ and to $L$ at $X$, gives
$$\kappa_X[a]\,s_{QX}\,H_D(t_X)=t_{HX}\,Q(e_X)\,\kappa_{X[a]}.$$
Here is the composition check: first use naturality of $\bar e_P$ at $\varphi_{L,X}$ to move $P_D(\varphi_{L,X})[a]$ past $\bar e_P$; the $L$ shift equation replaces $\varphi_{L,X}[a]\bar e_{L,QX}L_D(t_X)$ by $t^{\mathcal B}_{C(L)X}Q_{\mathcal B}(e_{L,X})\varphi_{L,X[a]}$. Next use the $P$ shift equation at $C(L)X$, replacing $\varphi_{P,C(L)X}[a]\bar e_{P,Q_{\mathcal B}C(L)X}P_D(t^{\mathcal B}_{C(L)X})$ by $t_{HX}Q(e_{P,C(L)X})\varphi_{P,(C(L)X)[a]}$. Finally naturality of $\varphi_P$ at $e_{L,X}$ replaces $\varphi_{P,(C(L)X)[a]}P_DQ_{\mathcal B}(e_{L,X})$ by $QC(P)(e_{L,X})\varphi_{P,C(L)(X[a])}$. The remaining factors are exactly $Q(e_X)$ and $\kappa_{X[a]}$.

source.place: paragraph on adjunction units and counits; agent expansion, step 4

proof.text:
Naturality of $\eta^D$ at $t_X$ gives $\eta^D_{(QX)[a]}t_X=H_D(t_X)\eta^D_{Q(X[a])}$. Therefore steps 2--4 and naturality of $t$ at $u_X$ give the following typed chain:
$$\begin{aligned}
\kappa_X[a]s_{QX}\eta^D_{(QX)[a]}t_X
&=t_{HX}Q(e_X)\kappa_{X[a]}\eta^D_{Q(X[a])}\\
&=t_{HX}Q(e_Xu_{X[a]})\\
&=t_{HX}Q(u_X[a])\\
&=Q(u_X)[a]t_X\\
&=\kappa_X[a](\eta^D_{QX})[a]t_X.
\end{aligned}$$
Cancel the isomorphisms $\kappa_X[a]$ and $t_X$ to obtain the requested equation at every object $QX$. The two sides are natural transformations from $[a]$ to $[a]\circ H_D$ (composition of functors read right to left). Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], for the cochain localization $Q$ at quasi-isomorphisms of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], now makes them equal on all of $D(\mathcal A)$. Exactness is used only through the cited exact-functor factorization; no boundedness or resolution assumption occurs.
